name: BTC Attack34a weekly break H1
description: Weekly break-and-hold, the direct consequence of Attack 33's diagnostic. Entry: first close above the PRIOR COMPLETED WEEK'S HIGH. Stop: the prior week's LOW - genuine structure. 2R fixed, 4-week hold cap. Claims that a decisive break of the prior week's high marks continuation at a timeframe where real positioning happens, rather than at an arbitrary rolling extreme. Honest about family: shares breakout DNA with Attack 33, but differs in LEVEL TYPE (calendar-anchored, not rolling) and FREQUENCY - the variable Attack 33 proved decisive. Bare: no trend, volatility, session or cooldown filter. This is the NEVER-TUNED half, the one that decides discard or advance.
notes: BOTH HALVES CLEAR 1.0 - THE FIRST MECHANISM IN THIS LAB'S HISTORY TO DO SO. 34a (never-tuned, 2022-01-01 to 2024-06-08): PF 1.48290761 / DD 46.88451809% / 30 trades / 50.00% win / +55.93% / commission $292.22. 34b (recent): PF 1.13703696 / DD 32.24854336% / 23 trades / 43.48% win / +14.20% / commission $243.50. THE FREQUENCY FIX WORKED COMPLETELY: $292 and $243 of commission against Attack 33's $6,460.27 on 757 trades. The cost problem that killed Attack 33 is solved. AND THE TENSION REGISTERED BEFORE THE RUN IS EXACTLY WHAT HAPPENED. The Pine header stated in advance: 'the low-frequency fix for the cost problem runs straight into the sample floor'. 34a lands on EXACTLY 30 trades - the thinnest possible pass of RATCHET v2 clause 3 - and 34b's 23 trades is BELOW it. So 1.13703696 on 23 trades is a DIRECTION, not a result, and is not quoted as one (LESSON 12). VERDICT: ADVANCES by the mandate's own words, since both halves cleared 1.0 - but as the WEAKEST POSSIBLE ADVANCE. One half sits at the floor, one below it, and the drawdowns are severe: 46.88% and 32.25%, against 3M's verified champion at 8.73%. A strategy losing nearly half its equity is not tradeable regardless of profit factor. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING IS BIGGER THAN THE MECHANISM: on 4.7 years of 15m data a strategy apparently cannot be BOTH cheap enough to be profitable AND frequent enough to be provable. Attack 33 had 757 trades and died on costs; Attack 34 is cost-free and cannot reach a sample. That is a constraint on the whole search, not on either candidate, and it was predicted in writing before this run rather than discovered afterwards.

name: BTC Attack35a weekly break 1.5R H1
description: Attack 34's weekly break-and-hold with the ONLY change being reward:risk cut from 2.0 to 1.5. Entry and stop byte-identical to Attack 34 (first close above the prior completed week's high; stop at the prior completed week's low). Motivated by Attack 34's own mandate-required audit: the disqualifying number is drawdown, not profit factor, and the mandate asks for exit/risk changes (target multiple, hold cap, stop reference) before new entry filters. Pre-registered rationale verified against Attack 34a's real trade log via get_trades: trade #1 (entry 39502.5, R=4012) ran up $6,422 in price before reversing to its eventual stop-out -- MORE than a 1.5R target distance (6018) but LESS than 2R (8024) -- so a nearer target would have closed that exact trade as a win instead of a full loss. An R ceiling was considered and rejected first: every streak-driving loser in 34a's 2022 drawdown sat at 8-10% R, below where any sane ceiling would cut, while the trade a ceiling would remove (34a #27, R~15.3%) was the single best winner in the set.
notes: REVERTED - RATCHET v2 clause 1 fails on both halves. 35a: PF 1.277564 / DD 45.81833173% / 31 trades / 54.84% win / +32.85% / commission $286.09, against Attack 34a's PF 1.48290761 / DD 46.88451809% / 30 trades. PF fell (1.483 -> 1.278) while DD improved only 1.07pp (46.88% -> 45.82%). 35b: PF 1.08255083 / DD 32.24854336% / 24 trades / 45.83% win / +8.50% / commission $240.68, against Attack 34b's PF 1.13703696 / DD 32.24854336% / 23 trades. PF fell (1.137 -> 1.083) and DD was IDENTICAL TO THE CENT to Attack 34b's (32.24854336% both times). THE FINDING THAT SURVIVES THE REVERT: a change that can only move the TARGET exit price left H2's drawdown-setting trade completely untouched, which means that trade was a STOP-LOSS, not a shortened winner. Attack 34's drawdown is set by the stop side of the trade, not the target side. Target multiple is eliminated as a lever for this mechanism's drawdown -- recorded so no future cycle re-spends credits re-testing it. Trade count also moved (30->31, 23->24) despite byte-identical entry logic, confirming the count is not perfectly deterministic run-to-run at this sample size (a small number of trades sit exactly on the window boundary) rather than any entry-logic difference.

name: Attack 36a: narrow-range day expansion, NEVER-TUNED half
description: Discovery mechanism #4 (numbered 36 after the cloud routine claimed 35 for a 1.5R sweep on Attack 34) for the invented lab, and the first aimed at the board's OWN stated queue item: 'the 46.88% drawdown is the disqualifying number, not the profit factor.' Claim: a day whose range contracts below 70% of its ~20-day mean is storing an imbalance that the first close above that compressed day's high resolves directionally. Distinct from all three predecessors -- VWAP (an intraday mean, retired), Attack 33 (a rolling N-bar extreme), Attack 34 (a calendar level) -- because the price event is secondary to a VOLATILITY STATE. Stop at the compressed day's low, so R is small BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by filtering.
notes: NUMBERING: run as "Attack 35" locally, renumbered to 36 on merge -- the cloud routine independently claimed 35 the same hour for a 1.5R target sweep on Attack 34 (PF 1.277564/31 and 1.08255083/24, REVERTED because it does not touch the drawdown). Same collision class as the v50 clash. DISCARDED by the kill rule registered in the Pine header BEFORE the run: the never-tuned half came in at 0.83969095, below 1.0, so no filter stack was added and the second half was never run. THE RISK-GEOMETRY FIX WORKED AND THE EDGE STILL DID NOT EXIST -- and separating those two things is the finding. Average loser -$208.33 against Attack 34's -$772, so the tight structural stop cut per-trade risk by roughly 4x exactly as designed. Drawdown still came in at 52.83%, WORSE than Attack 34's 46.88%, because it accumulated from a steady bleed (-26.05% net on a 33.90% win rate) rather than from a few large losses. SHRINKING R DOES NOT FIX A DRAWDOWN CAUSED BY A NEGATIVE EDGE, and the board's queue item 3 -- 'judge successors on drawdown first' -- is therefore only half a criterion: drawdown has to be read together with WHERE it came from. Cost was never the issue here either ($989 across 118 trades, versus Attack 33's $6,460 across 757), so the frequency window between Attack 33 and Attack 34 is confirmed workable and is not what killed this.

name: Attack 37a: liquidity sweep reversal, NEVER-TUNED half
description: Discovery mechanism #5 for the invented lab (numbered 37, continuing after 36). Claim: a break below a prior 20-bar swing low that FAILS -- the same bar closes back above that level -- is a stop-run liquidity sweep rather than genuine new supply, and price mean-reverts upward because the breakdown lacked conviction. The first REVERSAL/fade mechanism tried under the new mandate; Attacks 33/34/36 all traded WITH their breakout direction. Stop at the sweep bar's own low (the actual flush extreme), so R is set by wick depth rather than by a weekly range or a compressed day's range. Related in idea-space to the old cycle 003 (LCR-1, liquidation cascade reclaim, REJECTED PF 0.69 on 5m under the pre-2026-09-02 mandate) but a different, minimal two-term construction with no volume/range filter, tested for the first time under the 15m split protocol.
notes: BOTH HALVES CLEAR 1.0 -- the second mechanism ever to do so under the discovery mandate, after Attack 34. 37a (never-tuned, 2022-01-01 to 2024-06-08): PF 1.02423271 / DD 31.63538941% / 322 trades / 38.20% win / avg loser -$116.19 / avg winner $192.53 / +5.60% / commission $2,845.60. 37b (recent, 2024-06-08 to 2026-09-01): PF 1.01155847 / DD 24.31004442% / 196 trades / 37.24% win / avg loser -$127.81 / avg winner $217.83 / +1.82% / commission $2,006.22. MUCH WEAKER PF MARGIN THAN ATTACK 34 (1.483/1.137) -- both halves sit within 2.5% of break-even, which on this sample size (322 and 196 trades, both above the ~30-trade floor, LESSON 12 satisfied) is a real but thin edge, not noise, but it is not a strong one. THE DRAWDOWN SOURCE, PER THE SHARPENED CRITERION FROM ATTACK 36: avg loser is 6x smaller than Attack 34's (-$116/-$128 vs -$772) and largest single loss ($620.77 / $284.38) is nowhere near the max drawdown -- so like Attack 36 this is a BLEED-type drawdown (accumulated from many small losses, not a few large ones), not a large-R sizing problem. UNLIKE ATTACK 36, the edge underneath the bleed is genuinely positive (PF>1) on both halves rather than negative -- so Attack 36's disqualifier ('shrinking R does not fix a drawdown caused by a negative edge') does not apply verbatim here. What this run actually shows is a THIRD drawdown category the board has not named yet: a thin-but-real positive edge, traded at high frequency and 100%-of-equity compounding with a sub-40% win rate, still produces a large %-drawdown from ordinary streak variance even with no single catastrophic loss and no negative edge. Max drawdown is smaller than Attack 34's on H1 (31.64% vs 46.88%) and comparable on H2 (24.31% vs 32.25%). Still UNTRADEABLE at 24-32% DD -- this is not a champion. Per the mandate's own words both halves clearing 1.0 means it EARNS a filter stack (e.g. a regime/session filter aimed at the streaky losing stretches, since R is already about as small as this construction allows) -- queued for the next cycle, NOT built this cycle: two backtests were run per the credit budget (626 credits, 'above 500 the full pair, never more than two runs') and both are spent on the bare-mechanism pair itself, exactly as the mandate specifies for a first pass.
